A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TextResNet study and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–G. Retained material and the additions to v2 can be reliably matched.

before.justification: V1 reports original evaluations on four benchmarks, component ablations, attribution analyses, and experiments on chain depth, backward models, scheduling, and token consumption.

after.justification: V2 retains these empirical results and adds heterogeneous-model evaluations, human annotations of feedback failures, prompt-evolution measurements, and an OPTIMAS cost comparison.

M1.justification: The additive forward state, Semantic Projector, causal routing, density-based scheduler, and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. Section 4.2 clarifies the identity highway as dictionary updates and field selection, already documented in v1, rather than introducing a different procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use HotpotQA, BigCodeBench, PubMedQA, and STaRK-Prime with the same task coverage. The new appendix studies analyze retained tasks and change model configurations or measurement procedures, without adding a distinct dataset or task domain.

E2.justification: The Table 1 comparator set is unchanged. Whereas v1 discusses but excludes OPTIMAS from evaluation, v2 adds an appendix comparison: a truncated HotpotQA run and cost-normalized HotpotQA and BigCodeBench results in F.9/Table 10.

E3.justification: New protocols include mixed forward/backward model assignments, annotation of 50 HotpotQA trajectories by four annotators, normalized Levenshtein measurements at specified optimization snapshots, and budget-limited OPTIMAS evaluation with gain-per-cost metrics. These substantially extend the evaluation design; the original benchmark settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: F.6–F.9 substantially expand the analyses with cross-family and mixed-forward robustness, annotated failure-mode frequencies and a concrete feedback trace, prompt-evolution analysis, and cost-normalized comparisons. The earlier backward-model sweep, depth experiments, scheduling ablations, and token analysis are retained rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: F.7 adds limited annotation-reliability reporting: independent judgments from four annotators, majority-vote consolidation, and only one reported disagreement before discussion. Existing seed information, three test repeats, and uncertainty displays remain unchanged; the additions provide no formal agreement coefficient or confidence intervals.

E6.justification: Main benchmark and ablation scores remain unchanged, but substantial new results appear in Tables 7–10. Examples include 45.10 and 44.80 F1 for added heterogeneous configurations, approximately 35% versus 5% signal blockage for TextGrad versus TextResNet, prompt-edit distances of 0.416/0.150/0.049, and cost-normalized OPTIMAS comparisons. These are additional results, not improved scores for the original configuration.

T1.justification: The existing definitions, propositions, assumptions, and Appendix D derivations are unchanged. F.9 adds Equation 19, explicitly defining the new cost-normalized gain relative to TextGrad; it introduces no new theoretical guarantee.

C1.justification: The introduction narrows the forward-pass claim from preventing signal blockage to reducing it, and the conclusion describes semantic entanglement as a root cause rather than the root cause. The abstract, four principal contributions, and overall performance and stability claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Interpretation and applicability receive substantial additions. F.5 distinguishes attribution-path depth from component dependency strength; Section 4.4 calls gradient density a practical proxy rather than an unbiased estimator. F.8 and G add evidence, model-capacity, and inspectable-state limitations, while F.6 and F.9 discuss mixed-model failures and qualifications on cost comparisons.

D1.justification: V2 documents model-role assignments and alternation for the heterogeneous experiments, annotation procedures, and GPU, runtime, and accounting assumptions for the cost comparison. The original implementation configurations, prompt templates, context-management details, and code-access statement are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds references including Yu et al. (2014), Pan et al. (2016), Guo et al. (2025), Lu et al. (2024), and BeCAME. F.9 expands the cost and complementarity discussion with OPTIMAS, while the central research positioning and novelty claim remain.

P1.justification: Changes include targeted introductory and concluding rewrites, clearer identity-highway and scheduler explanations, new Appendix F subsections, and updated affiliations, publication information, and acknowledgments. The main section sequence and most existing prose are retained.

P2.justification: V2 adds four compact appendix tables, Tables 7–10, and reflows surrounding material. Figure 10 moves upward within its page, and existing table placement changes locally. The original diagrams, plots, and table structures are otherwise retained.

improvement.justification: The feedback annotations and concrete example provide more direct support for the central failure-mode explanation, while heterogeneous-model checks and new applicability qualifications strengthen validation and clarity. The gains are limited by approximate failure percentages without explicit message counts and incompletely specified cost comparisons. The revision improves supporting evidence without substantially changing the method or original benchmark evidence.
